name: George Washington
alt: An oil painting of an older man with white powdered hair, wearing a dark coat against a plain background.
facts: He led an army of ordinary colonists to victory in the war that won independence for a brand-new country.
He could have stayed in the top job as long as he wanted, but chose to step down after two terms, setting an example future leaders followed for over a century.
He never got to live in the famous house built for the country's leaders to live and work in — it wasn't finished until after he left office.

name: John Adams
alt: An oil painting of a stout man with white hair pulled back, wearing a dark coat and white cravat.
facts: He spent years serving as a diplomat in Europe, helping convince other countries to support the fight for independence.
He and the man who beat him for a second term became bitter political rivals, then reconciled later in life and wrote each other letters for years.
He died on the 4th of July, fifty years to the day after a famous document was signed — and so did his old rival, on the very same day.

name: Thomas Jefferson
alt: An oil painting of a man with reddish hair swept back, wearing a dark coat in front of a warm brown background.
facts: He wrote the document that explained why a group of colonies wanted to break away and govern themselves.
He roughly doubled the size of the young country by purchasing a huge stretch of land from France.
He designed his own mountaintop home and filled it with inventions and gadgets he tinkered with himself.

name: James Madison
alt: An oil painting of a small, slender man with white hair, wearing a dark coat in front of a deep red curtain.
facts: He's remembered as the main architect behind the country's founding rulebook, helping write much of it himself.
He was the shortest and lightest person to ever hold the job, reportedly standing only about 5 foot 4.
During a war with Britain, enemy troops set fire to the home where he worked and lived, and his wife famously saved a painting of an earlier leader before fleeing.

name: James Monroe
alt: An oil painting of a man with gray hair brushed back, wearing a dark coat against a muted brown background.
facts: His time in office became known for such political calm that historians later nicknamed it after good feelings.
He issued a famous warning telling European powers to stay out of the Americas, a stance that shaped foreign policy for generations.
He was the last one of these leaders to have fought in the war for independence as a young soldier, and was wounded in an early battle.

name: John Quincy Adams
alt: A portrait of a balding man with graying hair, wearing a dark coat and white collar.
facts: His father had held the very same job decades earlier, making them the first father-and-son pair to do so.
After losing his bid for a second term, he spent nearly two decades representing his district in the House, the only one of these leaders to do that.
He argued a case before the country's highest court that helped a group of freed, kidnapped Africans win their freedom.

name: Andrew Jackson
alt: An oil painting of a sharp-featured man with thick white hair, wearing a dark coat with a red collar.
facts: He survived a duel years earlier with a bullet lodged near his heart that doctors never removed.
He was the first one of these leaders to have been born in a log cabin rather than wealth and privilege.
An assassin's pistols both misfired when aimed at him at close range, and he reportedly fought back by beating the man with his cane.

name: Martin Van Buren
alt: An oil painting of a balding man with light, wispy hair, dressed in formal dark clothing.
facts: He was the first one of these leaders who had been born a citizen of the new country rather than a subject of Britain.
He helped build one of the country's first major political parties, organizing it almost like a modern campaign machine.
Growing up in a small New York town, his first language at home was Dutch, not English.

name: William Henry Harrison
alt: An oil painting of an older man with gray hair, wearing a dark coat and high collar.
facts: He served the shortest time in the job of anyone who's ever held it — about a month.
He gave the longest inaugural speech in the country's history, over two hours long, outdoors in cold, wet weather.
He first became famous as a general, winning a battle named after a river that became his lifelong nickname.

name: John Tyler
alt: A portrait of a slim man with light, swept-back hair, wearing a dark coat and bow tie.
facts: He suddenly took over the top job after his predecessor died just a month into the term, the first time that had ever happened.
He had more children than anyone who's held the position — fifteen in total, from two marriages.
Decades after leaving office, he sided with a breakaway group of states and was elected to their legislature, though he died before he could take his seat.

name: James K. Polk
alt: An old black-and-white photo of a serious-looking man with hair swept back, wearing a dark coat.
facts: He promised voters he'd serve only one term, and then he actually kept that promise and retired.
During his four years in office, the country's territory grew by roughly a third, including a stretch of the Pacific coast.
He worked so relentlessly at his desk that he rarely took vacations, and historians think it wore down his health badly — he died just months after leaving office.

name: Zachary Taylor
alt: An old photograph of a weathered-looking older man with short hair, dressed in dark formal clothing.
facts: He was a career military general, nicknamed for being tough as old wood, before he ever ran for the top office.
He had never even voted in a presidential election before he was elected to the job himself.
He died suddenly of a stomach illness after just sixteen months in office.

name: Millard Fillmore
alt: A black-and-white photo of a clean-shaven man with neat hair, wearing a dark coat and high collar.
facts: He grew up so poor that he was apprenticed to a cloth-maker as a teenager before teaching himself law.
During his term, the country opened up trade with an island nation that had kept its ports closed to the West for centuries.
He later turned down an honorary degree from a famous English university, joking he hadn't had the classical schooling to deserve it.

name: Franklin Pierce
alt: A black-and-white photo of a clean-shaven man with wavy dark hair, gazing slightly to the side.
facts: Weeks before he took office, he survived a train derailment that killed his young son right in front of him.
He was a war hero who, despite a painful injury, refused to leave his troops on the battlefield.
His personal struggles with grief and heavy drinking are now widely seen by historians as having overshadowed his time in office.

name: James Buchanan
alt: A black-and-white photo of an older man with white hair and a high white collar.
facts: He remains the only one of these leaders to never marry.
One of his eyes saw close-up well and the other was better for distance, so he developed a habit of tilting his head depending on what he looked at.
He watched the country splinter apart during his final months in office and openly admitted he didn't know how to stop it.

name: Abraham Lincoln
alt: A black-and-white photo of a tall, gaunt man with a distinctive beard along his jawline.
facts: He taught himself law and grammar largely by reading borrowed books late at night by candlelight.
He led the country through its bloodiest war and issued an order that began freeing millions of enslaved people.
He was the first one of these leaders to be assassinated, shot at a theater just days after the war finally ended.

name: Andrew Johnson
alt: A black-and-white photo of a clean-shaven man with dark hair, wearing a dark coat and bow tie.
facts: He never attended school a single day in his life and taught himself to read as a young tailor's apprentice.
He became the first one of these leaders to be impeached, though the Senate fell one vote short of removing him.
He returned to government years after leaving office, becoming the only former one of these leaders to later serve in the Senate.

name: Ulysses S. Grant
alt: A black-and-white photo of a bearded man in a dark coat, looking directly at the camera.
facts: He commanded the winning side's armies in a brutal civil war before he ever held political office.
After leaving office, he traveled around the entire world for over two years, drawing huge crowds wherever he went.
Dying of cancer, he raced to finish writing his memoirs, completing them just days before he died.

name: Rutherford B. Hayes
alt: A sepia-toned photo of an older man with a long, full beard.
facts: He won an incredibly disputed election that had to be settled by a special commission instead of a normal vote count.
He promised ahead of time to serve only one term, and he stuck to that promise.
At his wife's request, alcohol was banned from formal dinners at the place where he lived and worked.

name: James A. Garfield
alt: A black-and-white photo of a bearded man resting his hand near his chin.
facts: He's the only one of these leaders to have also worked as a college president before entering politics.
He partly paid his own way through college by working as the school's janitor and bell-ringer.
He was shot by a disappointed office-seeker just months into his term and suffered for weeks before dying from the wound.

name: Chester A. Arthur
alt: A sepia-toned photo of a mustached man with neatly combed hair, dressed sharply.
facts: He was a fairly obscure party insider before suddenly being thrust into the top job after a shocking assassination.
Surprising his own old political allies, he championed a law that overhauled how government jobs were handed out, weakening the favor-trading system that had helped his own career.
He was such a snappy dresser that he reportedly owned more than 80 pairs of trousers and changed outfits several times a day.

name: Grover Cleveland
alt: A black-and-white photo of a heavyset man with a thick mustache.
facts: He's one of only two of these leaders to serve two terms that weren't back-to-back, leaving office and then winning again four years later.
He got married in the very house where he lived and worked, the only wedding of its kind ever held there.
He secretly had surgery on a friend's yacht to remove a tumor from his mouth, keeping it hidden from the public for decades.

name: Benjamin Harrison
alt: A black-and-white photo of an older man with a short, full beard.
facts: He was the grandson of another man who had briefly held the very same job decades earlier.
Electric lighting was installed in the place he lived and worked for the first time during his term, though he and his family were reportedly nervous about touching the switches.
He lost his bid for a second term to the very same opponent he had defeated four years earlier.

name: William McKinley
alt: A black-and-white photo of a clean-shaven man with thinning hair, wearing a dark formal coat.
facts: He was the first one of these leaders to campaign by telephone, fielding calls from his own front porch instead of touring the country.
He carried a red flower as a personal good-luck charm and had just given it away to a young girl moments before he was shot.
He was shot by an anarchist while greeting a long line of well-wishers at a public fair.

name: Theodore Roosevelt
alt: A black-and-white photo of a mustached man wearing round spectacles.
facts: He became the youngest person ever to hold the top job after a sudden assassination put him in charge at just 42.
An avid outdoorsman, he helped create the country's national park system and once survived a shooting during a campaign speech, then finished the speech anyway with the bullet still in his chest.
He won a major international peace prize for helping end a war between two other countries.

name: William Howard Taft
alt: A sepia-toned photo of a large, mustached man dressed in formal attire.
facts: He's the only one of these leaders to later go on to lead the country's highest court after his time as its top political leader.
He was large enough that a specially built, oversized bathtub — big enough for four average-sized men — was installed for him where he lived and worked.
He started the tradition of throwing out the first ceremonial pitch at a baseball game.

name: Woodrow Wilson
alt: A black-and-white photo of a thin-faced man wearing wire-rimmed glasses.
facts: He led the country through a major world war and helped design an international organization meant to prevent future ones.
He suffered a severe stroke in office that left him partly paralyzed, and his wife secretly helped manage many of his duties afterward.
Before politics, he was a university president, and he remains the only one of these leaders to also hold a doctorate degree.

name: Warren G. Harding
alt: A formal portrait photo of a silver-haired man with a strong jaw, dressed in a dark suit.
facts: He promised a return to simpler, calmer times after a difficult world war, using a catchy slogan about getting back to normal.
He died suddenly of a heart attack while still in office, during a long cross-country speaking trip.
Scandals involving corrupt associates in his administration came to light only after his death, badly damaging his reputation.

name: Calvin Coolidge
alt: A black-and-white photo of a thin-faced man with neatly parted hair, looking off to the side.
facts: He earned a famous nickname for being a man of remarkably few words, even at his own dinner parties.
He was sworn in by his own father, a small-town notary public, by lamplight in their family farmhouse after his predecessor died suddenly.
He kept a pet raccoon and several other animals as part of a small menagerie at the place he lived and worked.

name: Herbert Hoover
alt: A black-and-white photo of a round-faced man in a dark suit and tie.
facts: Before entering politics, he made a fortune as a mining engineer working on projects around the world.
He took office just months before a massive stock market crash plunged the country into its worst economic crisis.
Years earlier, he had organized huge international relief efforts that fed millions of starving people in Europe after a world war.

name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
alt: A black-and-white photo of a silver-haired man in a dark suit, looking slightly upward with a determined expression.
facts: He's the only one of these leaders ever elected to the job four separate times.
He lost the use of his legs to a paralyzing illness years before taking office, but rarely let the public see him using a wheelchair.
He led the country through both its worst economic crisis and a second world war, working from the same desk through both.

name: Harry S. Truman
alt: A color portrait of a silver-haired man wearing glasses and a dark suit.
facts: He had no college degree, unlike most who've held the job, and once ran a men's clothing store before entering politics.
He had to make the decision to use a devastating new weapon to help end a world war.
He kept a sign on his desk reminding everyone that responsibility for the toughest decisions stopped with him.

name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
alt: A color photo of a balding older man with a broad smile, wearing a dark suit.
facts: He commanded the allied forces that stormed the beaches of Europe to help defeat a wartime enemy.
On his way out of office, he famously warned about the dangers of letting military spending grow too powerful and unchecked.
He helped start construction of the country's massive highway system, partly inspired by road networks he'd seen used by his old wartime rivals.

name: John F. Kennedy
alt: A color photo of a young, dark-haired man smiling, dressed in a dark suit.
facts: He's the youngest person ever elected to the job, and also one of the youngest to die in it.
He challenged the country to land people on the moon before the end of the decade, even though the technology to do it didn't exist yet.
He was assassinated while riding in a parade through a Texas city, an event watched and replayed on television by millions.

name: Lyndon B. Johnson
alt: A black-and-white photo of a tall man with large ears, wearing a dark suit.
facts: He took the oath of office aboard an airplane just hours after his predecessor was assassinated.
He pushed through sweeping laws banning racial discrimination, even though he knew it would cost his political party support in parts of the country.
He chose not to run for another term while an unpopular war overseas dragged on and divided the country.

name: Richard Nixon
alt: A color portrait of a dark-haired man with a serious expression, standing in front of a flag.
facts: He resigned from the job rather than face near-certain removal after a break-in scandal traced back to his own re-election team.
He's the only one of these leaders to resign from the job before finishing his term.
He opened formal relations with a huge country that had been isolated from the West for decades, surprising much of the world.

name: Gerald Ford
alt: A color photo of a silver-haired man smiling in front of a flag and an eagle emblem.
facts: He's the only one of these leaders never elected to either the top job or the second-in-command role, rising to the top spot through resignations rather than a vote.
He had been such a talented college football player that professional teams tried to recruit him.
He pardoned his disgraced predecessor just a month into his own term, a controversial move that may have cost him the next election.

name: Jimmy Carter
alt: A color photo of a smiling, light-haired man standing in front of striped flags.
facts: Before politics, he ran his family's peanut farm in a small Georgia town.
He brokered a historic peace agreement between two longtime rival nations in the Middle East, hosting marathon talks at a presidential retreat.
After leaving office, he spent decades building houses for families in need and later won a global peace prize for his humanitarian work.

name: Ronald Reagan
alt: A color portrait of a dark-haired older man smiling gently in front of a flag.
facts: He spent years as a Hollywood actor before turning to politics, eventually leading a major actors' union.
He survived being shot just months into his first term and reportedly joked with doctors right before surgery.
When he was first elected, he was the oldest person yet to win the job, leaving office in his late 70s.

name: George H. W. Bush
alt: A color photo of a silver-haired man smiling broadly in a dark suit.
facts: He flew dozens of combat missions as a Navy pilot in World War II and was shot down once over the Pacific.
He led the country's main intelligence agency before ever becoming its top political leader.
His son went on to hold the very same job decades later, making them only the second father-and-son pair in the country's history to do so.

name: Bill Clinton
alt: A color photo of a gray-haired man smiling widely in front of a flag and bookshelves.
facts: He became just the second one of these leaders to be impeached, though, like the first, he was not removed from office.
The federal budget was balanced for the first time in decades during his time in office.
He played the saxophone on a late-night talk show during his first campaign, surprising audiences with his musical side.

name: George W. Bush
alt: A color photo of a smiling man with short hair, standing in front of a flag.
facts: He was in office during a devastating terrorist attack on the country that reshaped American foreign policy for years.
He owned part of a Major League Baseball team before entering politics full time.
He's the second son of a former office-holder to win the very same job his father once held.

name: Barack Obama
alt: A color photo of a smiling man with short dark hair, standing in front of flags and curtains.
facts: He became the first Black person elected to lead the country.
He worked as a community organizer in Chicago before going into law and politics.
He won a major international peace prize less than a year into his first term, before most of his policies had even taken effect.

name: Donald Trump
alt: A color photo of a man with distinctive light-colored hair, wearing a dark suit and tie.
facts: Before politics, he spent decades as a real estate developer and hosted a reality television show about business competitions.
He left office, then later won election again four years afterward — only one earlier leader in the country's history had also pulled that off.
He was sworn in as the oldest person yet to take the oath for this job, and survived an assassination attempt at an outdoor rally just months earlier.

name: Joe Biden
alt: A color photo of a smiling white-haired man in a dark suit, standing in front of a flag.
facts: He served for decades as a senator before spending eight years as second-in-command to his predecessor.
When he first took the oath of office, he was the oldest person yet to do so, at 78 — a record broken by the very next person to hold the job.
He overcame a childhood stutter that he's spoken openly about throughout his career.
